# descope_auth_access_rule (Resource)

Manages a single rule of the project's auth access policy. Rules are evaluated in the order set by the `descope_auth_access_policy` resource, and the first rule whose conditions all match decides whether the authentication is allowed or blocked.



<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `effect` (String) Whether an authentication that matches the rule is `allow`ed or `block`ed.
- `project_id` (String) The ID of the project that this rule belongs to. Changing this value will require the resource to be deleted and recreated.

### Optional

- `conditions` (Attributes List) The conditions that must all match for the rule to apply. A rule with no conditions matches every authentication. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--conditions))
- `description` (String) An optional description of what the rule is for.
- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether the rule is evaluated. A disabled rule keeps its place in the evaluation order but never matches.
- `expire_time` (Number) The time after which the rule is no longer evaluated, in seconds since the Unix epoch. Set to `0` for a rule that never expires.
- `name` (String) A name for the rule, shown in the console.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The ID of this resource.

<a id="nestedatt--conditions"></a>
### Nested Schema for `conditions`

Required:

- `key` (String) The attribute the condition checks. One of `request.ip`, `request.country`, `user.email`, `user.emailDomain`, `user.loginId` or `user.phone`.
- `operator` (String) How the attribute is compared with the values. One of `equal`, `notEqual`, `in`, `notIn`, `inCidr` or `notInCidr`. The CIDR operators are only supported with the `request.ip` key.
- `values` (List of String) The values to compare with. The `equal`, `notEqual`, `inCidr` and `notInCidr` operators take exactly one value. With `equal` and `notEqual` the value may instead be a reference of the form `{{jwtClaims.<name>}}`, which compares the attribute with that custom claim of the token the user presented. An absent claim never matches. Values must be in canonical form: lowercase emails and domains, uppercase country codes, phone numbers in E.164 form and IP addresses in their shortest form.
